t:
You are familiar with magic, but there are worlds where instead of full-flowing rivers you can find only drying up streams. The magic in those worlds is the gift of a select few. Such is this world - there is enough progress, but very little magic. But there's a problem: a race of demon-like creatures from the worlds of chaos settled there. Invisible to most, they would freely enter it and commit unthinkable atrocities, if it weren't for the chosen ones who, due to a strange whim of the gods who created that world, turned out to be teenage girls.

It was they who received the magical gift, and it was they who were chosen to fight against the creatures of Chaos hiding in the shadows. No one in that world is aware of the threat that hangs over everyone, no one knows the names of the real defenders of that land.

The worlds that lost their patrons or never had them suffer the most. They are under constant threat from technically advanced outer worlds.

All-Mother never supposed that mortals of the outer worlds would be able to travel between them. But Nihaz has altered the Great Circle cycle, enabling many worlds to live beyond their lifespan - and to travel. Sadly, this didn't make their lives any better. Having reached the pinnacle of technical advancements, the worlds commonly fell prey to some disaster. They would either ruin themselves or had to face an external threat.

Yukmid is another world with very little magic. Albeit territorial division, they hardly ever made big wars. Their life would have been nice and easy if only a hostile civilization of aliens hadn't invaded Yukmid.

No one likes uninvited guests, as you understand. Just the same as we weren't happy to welcome you on Eden, dwellers of Yukmid were caught off guard. On top of everything else, the invaders thought it would be a good idea to slave the people of Yukmid. Their cities were under attack. The intruders, much more technically advanced, utterly routed Yukmid's army. It would have become a tragedy but a hero turned up.

You might say that heroes aren't equal to gods. But sometimes a hero can become a god. Are you familiar with the power of faith? What if a world's faith is focused in a single person? Would that change him, and how? All-Mother might have a better explanation. In any case, there was this hero in Yukmid. Everyone in the world could watch him via communication devices. As I said, there's next to no magic in this world but somehow the inhabitants' great faith in a single person imbued him with magical powers. He stopped the invasion army, killed their leaders, and destroyed all of their minions almost single-handedly.  Every victory increased Yukmid people's faith in him, giving him more and more power. He is praised more than anyone in this world.

You are a Sarnaut hero, aren't you? The faith of Sarnaut people could have been the secret of your success.

The universe is a dangerous place even without Nihaz. If it wasn't for monsters, there'd be no heroes... or patrons. The late Eons are dark times we know very little of.

There was a god of Darkness before Nihaz, as the legend would have it. Nobody remembers his name. He had been the adversary of Sarn the Light before All-Mother decided to recreate everything that has ever existed. The truth is that leftovers of the Forgotten army are still roaming in the darkness between worlds.

I came to know that the world of Zynn was building the Gates in order to travel between worlds, just like you did. However, they didn't have a Navigator, like you did. I'm talking about Skulnar. Zynn people had to wander blindly, randomly in the dark.

They managed to open the Gates. As bad luck would have it, madness gushed in. An ancient being from the shards of late Eons' worlds answered their call and sent its armadas through the Gates and into the world of Zynn.

The ancient darkness immediately swallowed the Gates. The ancient being subjugated everyone who was near. Its minions moved forward to take over the world of Zynn.
The All-Mother's power is the power of life itself. Life offers countless opportunities...
We are the children of progress People once fought with sticks and stones, now we have weapons that can affect even gods.
Hello! I'm sorry, but I'm a little bit busy right now. This Hopping Backpack is too powerful, and I need to reconfigure it...

Do you like it? I designed it together with one of the best Xadaganian engineers. Yes, don't look at me like that. We, scientists, don't care too much about squabbles between the Empire and the League.

This is called a Hopping Backpack. Well, he came up with the title, I don't usually give my inventions such obvious names. He also wanted to add some weird abbreviation - you know, Xadaganians always do that - but I did not let him.

Well, the title says everything. It is used for jumping. If you overload it, it jumps really far. We did it once and accidentally discovered a new allod... Now we are facing the music.

You know what I think? They really need manpower on that allod, and a Hopping Backpack would come in handy. Why don't you go there and help them? They would really appreciate that.
I am Humk! Uga-gash-kyrshylee! Goody-gods! No beat! Murk!
Grreat! Now let's get away from here. Don't let Tungars notice you. You can't fight them all!
At last! I thought you abandoned me!

You... You are right in time. They were about to slaughter me!

Your appearance was... extravagant. The savages were scared out of their minds! That was Murk's idea, wasn't it? I should give him a kiss when it's over.
I'd never thought I'd see a primitive savage ritual from the inside!

Ahem... You say that these Mechanoids look just like the Tep's minions that you saw on Irdrich. They were all destructed by some kind of mechanical impact. If there has been a fight, it was really long ago.

Look, their wreckages are arranged as if they were a trophy... Or an offering!

Maybe they were destroyed by that snow creature? Maybe Tep and his Mechanoids were those demons that Tungars are so afraid of? And they worship their icy god - a giant worm that... Where is it gone, by the way? I think it disappeared in a crack in the far corner of the cave.

Will you inspect it? I can't really walk yet. I hope they have a healer in the camp...

Oh great Tensess, give me patience...

I asked you to stay out of trouble, didn't I?! What have you done?! You slaughtered a whole camp of harmless local inhabitants! I... I don't even know what to say!

Alright, nevermind the savages. My wings are already blue from cold. You say they have warm tents? And a Portal? Huh... Well then, on behalf of all Surveyors, I express gratitude for the thorough genoc... I mean, assimilation of the hostile aborigines. We will study their cultural heritage later. We will send a couple... No, a squad of cultural experts on a research. And arrange a cultural patrol zone.

Come on, lead us to the camp before we turned into icicles!
Brrr! It's so cold! I wonder what the locals eat? Icicles for breakfast, ice fricasse for lunch, and snow soup for dinner?
Gyr! Baba! Tunga alala! Hohog oga?
Ferris is an inexhaustible source of mysteries. Who are these Tungars, for instance? Degraded goblins or evolved walruses? Nobody knows...

A meteorite on the bottom of the lake? Time travel to the past? A Xadaganian commander of an army of metal soldiers? What were Imperial soldiers doing here?

It was a closed allod! Neither the League nor the Empire knew of its existence! It could have made some sense if you'd seen Tep's servants. I'm sorry, but you story sounds more like a hallucination caused by hypothermia and suffocation.

No, no, and no! I'm not sending anyone to the lake to search for evidence of your hallucinations. We are under an emergency anyway - Elena, my precious muse, has gone!

You don't believe me? Ask Murk! He was the last one to see her!
I couldn't even imagine how many mysteries this tiny piece of unexplored land conceals. And we are the first ones to discover it! Isn't it amazing?

It was my shift on the watch. Me and Elena were supposed to patrol the camp perrimeter. She took on the northern part, and I took on the southern one. I frroze my tail off through the shift as I was supposed to, and then came back to the camp, but Elena wasn't there! Ay-hya! Me and Herbert have been rrunning off our legs since then, but still no sign of our beauty!
Aho! You owe me one, frriend! I sweated my back off when I was carrying you across the ice, while fighting off Tungars and lynxes!
Take this and don't lose it again!

Greetings! I've heard a lot about your deeds, and honestly, I'm happy that a hero like you is joining us for our research mission. I'm sure together we will find the answers to all the questions that are bothering you!

Now here is the deal. The Citadel's main weapon, the destructive beam, was eliminated, but there are still lots of bloodsuckers inside. Still the real threat comes from Amadeus, the spirit of the Citadel. I hope I can reprogram it. Our faith in Light will protect us from the darkness that has saturated these walls!

Are you with us?

Well... Our objective is quite simple - reach Ferris and find proofs of my tutor's hypotheses. As long as I've known him, the old man has never been wrong!

But nobody knows what is waiting for us on Ferris, so we have picked out the strongest and toughest historians. Our expedition is fully self-sustainable, so in case of any trouble we will deal with it on our own. Out team includes experienced fighters, keen hunters, and talented engineers... We are ready to face any unexpected circumstances!

I don't know much more than you do. Pridens don't have a developed writing system, so they pass on their history by word of mouth... Such an irresponsibility! This is just unbelievable.

Sorry, where was I... Well, one of the doolgas told us that Ferris is an extremely cold allod. Supposedly, it is completely covered with ice. We don't know what Tep's Cultists were doing there, or whether they were there at all. That's what we need to find out.

According to the coordinates that Zayan has calculated, Ferris is located quite close to the habitable lands of Sarnaut, but it is rather "deep". It is hard to believe that, but Ferris is probably one of the few stable objects in the deep layers of the Astral. And we will be the first ones to reveal its mysteries... Oh, I'm looking forward to this!
Off we go! The riddles of history are waiting for us!
Whoa! Now this is what I call a research mission. I'm so sick of burrowing among dusty manuscripts!
Aho, friend! I'm happy that we will shed our blood together, eysh!

Murk is not my real name. I am... an outcast. I rrefused to obey the Golas of my Brranch and left, giving up my name and my past. Though, frrankly, sometimes I miss Howlem, my homeland. But as the Historians say, everyone is the architect of their own happiness, zoor? I will build my own destiny, I swear on my ancestors!

Remember that mysterious amulet that I obtained after you returned from the captivity of illusions? I found out who it had belonged to. Long ago on Howlem, the distant land of Pridens, lived a tribe that Pridens called the Shoom Branch. One of Priden shamans - a doolga - told me that the Shoom Branch fell under the influence of Tep Cultists and was involved in one of his resurrection attempts, but eventually was obliterated by other Branches. It happened soon after the Shoom leader had discovered an ancient Portal that led to an allod unknown to Astralonauts. Pridens call it Ferris.

After those events Priden Golases completely sealed off their domain from the Astral net and isolated themselves from the rest of the world. This is why you don't usually see Pridens in the lands of the League or the Empire. They practically never leave their allod. But this is not the point.

It was not the legend that caught my interest, but Ferris itself. Don't you get it yet? Just think of it: somehow Tep gained almost a divine power. There is a projection of his own memories of the Shoom Pridens in his illusory world. Priden traitors joined the servants of the ancient summoner on an unknown allod. What conclusion can we draw? Ferris is the key to the understanding of the source of his power!

I wouldn't assert that Ferris is the place where Tep had gained his power. But something that happened there had been occupying his thoughts for sure. If we reach Ferris, we will find a key to this mystery!

I am a Great Mage. Maybe I'm not the strongest one, but I am the oldest. I remember our world being a single whole. I remember the horrors of the Cataclysm and the bloody years that followed. I saw cities coming down and houses burning, while thousands of mortals were dying for their governors' ambitions. When years and centuries pass you by and the world changes in front of your eyes, it is difficult to remain a detached observer, but I tried to... I do my best not to interfere! The ambitions of the Great Mages' have caused enough trouble to this world.

After I became a Historian, I swore not to interfere with the political affairs, not to play with the lives of mortals, and to stay away from the forbidden. My mission is to collect and to preserve. But can you imagine what will happen if the source of the divine power gets into the wrong hands?

And you... After all that you've been through, after you have faced the gods themselves, you will understand me better than anyone. This is why I'm asking you to help.

I have calculated the approximate coordinates of Ferris. It wasn't easy, but I did it. But if I'm guessing right, no regular ship can reach that Astral sector. Maybe Eclipse only... But whimsical Catherina is the last Great Mage I would share my mission with. It's enough she has almost ruined the whole Sarnaut because of her unreasonable ambitions!

You remember that Elves were involved in the construction of Eclipse? They have also built the Darkblood Citadel! The one that has almost turned my allod to ashes. It may be slower than Eclipse, but it's definitely way more solid. I'm sure you and my assistants will reach Ferris on it with no problem. You will only have to deal with the vampires swarming inside of it, and with crackpot Amadeus. My apprentice, Herbert, will help you. He will also lead the surveyors' expedition to Ferris.

Unfortunately, I cannot leave Avilon and go with you. Herbert is young and ardent, and you will be his right hand and his wise counselor.

Now go! I believe in the success of the expedition!
Excellent! Now let's assail the Citadel!
Greetings! It's been a long time since our last meeting... And many new riddles of the past have come about!
Wrong password. Premises sealed. Unauthorized access attempt reported to the security. Please remain on the spot and await your extermination.
Unauthorized access attempt detected. Please stop violating my intelligence and await your extermination.

I am Amadeus and I've been specifically created to work on this Darkblood Citadel.

I possess keen intuition and am fully conversational. Vocabulary - ten thousand words. Emotions deactivated. For detailed instructions see my developer - the Great Mage Gorluxor.

Confirm your status.
Hey there! I'm glad you are with us. They've written volumes about your adventures... And I've read them all!

There's not much to tell. I met the Historians in the times of the events on Asee-Teph. I was really distressed by what happened with the Tensess Temple and that traitor Gorluxor. I thought the Empire was utterly blemished by that treason, and asked the Historians to employ me and to give me a chance to prove that the Empire holds no grudge against them, but then I just loved the job. It's hard, but it's so interesting! Now history is my passion!

It turns out to be a journal covered in thick dirt. Once hard pages are now sodden and stick to the fingers like dough. Finally, the cover comes off from the pages. The first page is covered with writings and drawings - those are experiments' results and mysterious half-obliterated schemes.

But there are even more interesting inscriptions on the cover. It seems to be some kind of a code... Or a part of it. Maybe it will help us open the door to the Bestiary? Alas, there is no way to make it out...

We should search around. Maybe other scientists managed to escape and dropped some papers on the run. If we find more pieces with that code written on them, we will be able to retrieve it by parts.

The skeleton was wearing a tattered robe that resembles Imperial uniform of the scientists from the vision. The stained patch on the sleeve reads "Vasily Dankin". So he didn't manage to escape after all.

There is a square object under the scientists' bones. What could it possibly be?
Suspicious dents and scratches can be seen on the Mechanoid body. Looks like some giant beast tried to taste it. One should rather stay away from that creature.

The Mechanoid must have been lying here for not too long - its metal body hasn't even lost its polish. Seems like it was destroyed by the local automatic security system. There is nothing else peculiar about it.
Tep's technology is way too distinctive. This Mechanoid obviously belonged to his army.
The wreckage of the Imperial Mechanoid has been lying here for so long it got fleeced with moss and inhabited by an ant colony.
One shot from an Imperial Mechanoid was enough to put an end to the useless life of that Cultist.
Corpse of an Arisen dressed as a Tep Cultist. Good riddance.
On closer examination it turns out that some of the bones are missing, and the rest of them are gnawed by giant teeth. Still the cause of death cannot be determined.
A pile of decayed bones that, judging by the skull shape, belonged to an orc.
At least we don't have to wear skins anymore. I was itching all over as if I was sick or something, huh.

Haha, what are you saying? Oh, the "Gates"... I misheard you.

Nah, I don't know anything about it. But I would beat the hell out of those Cultists, you bet, huh! Have I told you that I used to work for Gorluxor? I was his personal guardian, that's right. And when he started his affair with Asee-Teph, that temple, I knew right away that it wasn't going to end well. So I pulled up stakes and took off as soon as you showed up, huh.

Honestly, I think that blasted necromancy will bite us all later. The Zems should have just stayed in their graves where they belonged. Take that Mekhdi. He pisses me off! He talks to me as if I were a dumb goblin. Next time he says something, I will kick him off the allod, I swear.

I've told you everything I knew. Sorry, I haven't found out anything new since.

After those kidnappings and your mysterious disappearance everyone in the camp has been watching after each other. I can feel someone's gaze on my back all the time. Either Murk, or Herbert, and now the Prowls, too. They are afraid to lose someone else, and I can understand that. But it's just impossible to work under such conditions!

And you know... It seems that Herbert... erm... has fallen in love with me. Don't get me wrong, he's a nice man in every respect... but I'm on duty! I don't know what to do about him.

I'm afraid I don't know much more than you do. And I don't like it!

After those kidnappings and your mysterious disappearance everyone in the camp has been watching after each other. They are afraid to lose someone else, and I can understand that. Everyone will be on their toes if anything happens.

Herbert has been keeping an eye on me. Sometimes it seems to me that... erm... he has fallen in love with me. Don't get me wrong, he's a nice man in every respect... but I'm on duty! We work together! I don't know what to do about him.
Weird things happen around. The more I know, the more I want to get away from here.

Oh, you've heard about my old hobby? I think some ships in the port of Novograd are still moored with my chains. I had to make a living somehow back in the day...

You say you need a chain? I guess I can help you with that. Watch and learn!
Finally! I thought we would have to stay in those frozen lands forever, lost in conjectures. I feel that we are close to very important discoveries!
Excellent! Wait a second, I'll charge the Mana Converter... Here you go! Runs like clockwork now. At least I hope so...
What... Where is Negus Jeeg? That filthy jackal that betrayed our Master? I will tear his heart out and feed it to desert centipedes, I swear on the three Pillars of Truth!

How dare you open your mouth in the presence of someone who has been through all the nine stages of torment? Impudent worm!

Answer me, slave, where is the Source? It must be somewhere near, and your stupid robots won't stop us! Jeeg - may his name be cursed! - has betrayed our Master! He fooled your stupid Nezeb, your dumb scientists, who thought they could fathom the divine nature of the Source... But he didn't fool us!

Where is the Source, slave?!
What?! I will tear your lying tongue out! One cannot deceive those who have seen the truth!
This place looks like a giant cemetery. I think we shouldn't have come to Ferris. Some mysteries should remain unraveled...

You want to know my opinion?

See, those barricades face the central area, which means they were purposed to protect the staff from something coming out of the Laboratory, not from the outside. Maybe the unknown enemy got inside through a Portal, maybe the Mechanoids went crazy, maybe... anything could have happened! We still don't have a clue.

But one thing I know for sure - this place should have remained secret. The Imperial scientists on the barricades clearly were not prepared to the assault.

quests: Поиски сокровищ: Память о том, что было

t:
As Sarbaz Baybut said, the Sanitation Zone is swarming with Mechanoids. They seem to attack any living being that they see. We could hardly make it to the barricades. Their defenders must have fought to the last.

You know, these barricades are giving me a lot of questions. They were clearly hastily improvised, and we still don't know, what the Imperial scientists were hiding from.

quests: Поиски сокровищ: Память о том, что было

t: Stop playing with the Mechanoid! Switch off and go inside.
The steel platform is quietly buzzing. It still preserves traces of old magic.
The steel platform is quietly buzzing. It still preserves traces of old magic.
The steel platform is quietly buzzing. It still preserves traces of old magic.
The steel platform is quietly buzzing. It still preserves traces of old magic.
Why are you here? Chasing me is pointless.

Well, you are not a master of provocation, but we should try.

I don't have time for personal squabbling. I can use the local resources to crush you like annoying flies.

You won't reach me and Herbert. We cannot let you, not now. We are preparing to enter a better world, a world free of your disgusting chaos. Our love will overcome all obstacles!
The steel platform is quietly buzzing. It still preserves traces of old magic.
Where would you like to go?
Here everything smells with rrot. And lies.

I don't know, kylys. I know that she is lying, and that you are playing along with her. Only a fool doesn't see that.

The question is, why are you doing this. If I find out that you are going to hurt Herbert or leave him behind, you will pay for that, rest assured. Everyone may have secrets, but as long as you don't mess with our mission, I don't care.

Am I being clear?

So... Zimina's clone, who possesses all her skills and memories, is walking around Ferris, threating the expedition and trying to reach some ancient device, for which the Empire once performed miracles of conspiracy? That's just great.

Zimina is right - it's about time we interfered. I will prepare a team of our best fighters and specialists. While I am working on that, you have to reconfigure the portal system on Ferris to let us teleport directly to you. Just don't let the Historians see it.

Is your mission clear? Go back. Let's not waste a minute!

The dark times continue! And every time you seem to be right in the thick of the events.

Everything is much more serious than I supposed. When I asked Herbert to keep his eye on the Historians, I hoped that they would find some crocks or writings that would help us learn more about the history of Sarnaut and Tep's life. But what you found... is unbelievable!

I will meet Izbor and Aidenus, take my best soldiers and set out to Ferris. You go back and don't let the Surveyors do anything stupid!
This echo gives me the chills...
What a weird material. Wait... What is going on?
It sounds like the elevator started working.
...The creature is silent. Its grotesque mask resembles a face and bears an expression of tranquility.

...The mask turns and slightly sinks, as if the Architect is actually looking at you. A ripple runs across its surface and the expression on the grotesque face slightly changes. It is... friendly?

The strange creature fills the room with quiet noise. Your ear doesn't recognize words, but they are imprinted in your consciousness in ice-cold letters:

"I am the Sculptor. Who are you?"

...The Sculptor is listening, slightly nodding his mask. Its emotions change each other rather unexpectedly and inaptly.

"You are seeking to unearth the secrets of those who were here before you. You have discovered the biggest one. They all died in the end, like they should have. And you destroyed what was left of them."

The Sculptor looks back at the portal. As he turns, an uncanny expression of triumph appears on his mask.

"They are me. We. No, me. The Architect."

...The Sculptor becomes silent and shuffles his giant leg-stilts, as if in confusion.

"They want me back. I don't want to go back - I fell off the Fractal. There is nothing for us... for me. I closed the Passage, but soon they will be back, they will come for me, and then you will go through the Ascent. You will be freed, sooner or later. We promise."

...An expression of surprise appears on the Sculptor's face. For the first time, he found the right expression.

"From Chaos, of course. You will become better, stronger and truer. You will be granted an infinite power - this is what the Ascent is. A Transmutation, if you wish. It is our mission. I hope you will forgive us for the delay. If I could, I would have furnished stronger resistance to your "Imperial scientists". I tried to transmute them, but now I see that eliminating would have been more effective. I am sorry."

...The Sculptor regretfully shakes his head.

...The mask smiles shortly, copying Marianne de Ardeur's manner. The Sculptor's words can be barely heard, as if he is speaking to himself.

"They all refused at first. Thousands of worlds, Chaos of million kinds - they all look alike. In your fear, you all preserve one Order."

...The Sculptor shivers, as if from a blow. The mask shows the expression of sheer bliss, and then frowns.

"I cannot handle them now. If they accept me, I will be no more. I cannot let this happen. I will die. I cannot die now."

...The Sculptor falls silent. Dozens of expressions change each other on his face. At some point, it becomes absolutely smooth, almost glassy. Another place can be seen through it - the World of the Architects.

Then the face appears again, serene.

...The Sculptor silently shakes his mask.

"I have been preparing your mind for a long time. The rest of the expedition will not endure my voice. You, too, cannot comprehend his design. We are the Architect. One day my words will make sense to you. One day, you will be touched by the Perfection."

...Solemn sound of his voice suddenly becomes softer.

"But I can try. I can feel that it is important for you."

...The mask slowly blinks.

"From the inside, of course. If you destroy it in the Fractal, it will be destroyed here as well."

...The Sculptor hesitates.

"If you destroy the Passage, they will not be able to enter this world. Your Ascent will be interrupted, and my mission will be failed. But my life will be saved. I feel... You have a word for this feeling. A strange word, a strange feeling... Dilemma."

...The Sculptor looks at you curiously. The mask has chosen the right emotion again.

"An offer? How interesting. And unexpected. I guess I don't have a choice?"

...The Architect draws himself up. Now his voice sounds triumphantly.

"May it be so. If my freedom costs your life in Chaos, it is your choice. I hope you realize what you are dooming yourself to."

It's hard to tell. First, we need to get finished with the expedition and report to everyone involved. I believe you are yet to face many dangers on your way. One of them is right in front of us - a door to another world!

I believe Marianne and that Imperial lady will handle this. They are determined to crush the whole army of the Architects! A difficult battle lies ahead of you, that's for sure. Consider your duty to the expedition fulfilled. Thank you for everything - we would have never made it without your help.

But... If you don't mind, I have one last request for you. I have written down my observations regarding the clone. Please, give it to Yaver Gnostis. He will storm me with questions if I meet with him personally, and I really don't feel like answering them.

January 11, 964

"The sudden death of Vasily Dankin has led to my appointment as the Head of the Research Complex. My little game has resulted in my full victory even earlier than I could imagine. Now all the staff are pawns in my hands... and Tep's hands. Soon their Sparks will follow that of Dankin. Soon. But not now. For now, I need them."

...

March 26, 964

"A Council agent has personally arrived to Ferris to supervise the development of the new ship prototype. I had no other choice but to demonstrate him the efficiency of the experimental ship reactor... Too bad he won't be able to tell anyone about it - there's just a handful of dust left of him. The Empire will have to cope without its new ships. Tep does not want the League to fall... I've just sent the schemes of experimental Mechanoids to my associates."

...

September 3, 964

"The Object seems to be hiding more mysteries than the Great Mages could have ever imagined... and neither could have Tep. Beyond all doubt, this is a source of a great power. I am finally on the right track."

April 11, 965

"I've heard Skrakan had found a way to fight demons. Now when all the eyes of the world are watching him, my hands are free. During the last year, I have gradually replaced all the members of the Gates research team. Now I can trust most of them, and the rest are just expendables - orcs, mostly. We don't have much time. The next few weeks are going to define the outcome of my operation."

...

April 18, 965

"The Object is barely responding to its surroundings. We keep recording weak splashes of energy, but still know too little about what is inside of it - a magical life form? An ancient mechanism? One of the "expendables" stated that he saw a weird light coming out of the Object at 4 a.m. on April, 15. We took note of his words and eliminated him before he had time to tell anyone else. (Reminder: assign writing an obitual.) We don't have the right to risk."

...

April 19, 965

...Another piece of paper is attached above the page. It must be a fragment of another Object research log. The researcher's hand-written notes cover a printed text.

"Inspection record #45. Numerous micro cracks have appeared on the surface of the Object (caused by the internal pressure. Of what?) On closer inspection, a dim blue light can be seen in the cracks, flashing at 36.3 second intervals (the color keeps changing within blue and green spectrum, depending on the surrounding noisiness). The interval slowly reduces (to 35.1 seconds in 9-hour observation). The Object produces a low humming and slightly vibrates, but does not respond to external irritants. Despite the obvious burst of activity, its temperature does not change and remains at the indoor level. All our attempts to heat or cool the Object were failed (try the experimental ship cannon?). End of record."

...

May 1, 965

"An undesired accident happened. While I was away, the Object came alive and tried to "make first contact", as Sarang Sargass put it. During 30 minutes, the Objects was producing series of low sounds, which became "progressively melodic and questioning" (?). The process started at 11:47 a.m., when the interval between the flashes, according to our calculations, had to come down to zero. After the supposed contact attempt, the blue light faded. The vibration and the humming stopped. The Object is giving no signs of activity."

June 30, 965

"Something weird is happening to my colleagues who have been working on the Object with me. First, Yasskul Tay and Sarbaz Korus went missing. And yesterday, I found Yaver Loku in the laboratory room, piercing herself with needles for bone sampling. When she saw me, she stretched her hands towards me and tried to say something, but her movement broke some of the needles, and suddenly she went into convulsion, hurting herself even more. I got rid of her body last night... And saw her again in the morning. In the security room. She was just standing there, staring into the surveillance camera screen, holding the head of the killed security orc in her hands (saw blue light in the eye pits). I paralyzed her and hid her in my room, tied by hands and leg. What is going on?"

...

September 19, 965

"Another body right in the middle of the main hall. Two bodies, to be more exact. A Xadaganian woman (laboratory technician from the agronomic department) and a goblin (shipyard mechanic). The Xadaganian's body and the goblin's head, jointed with strange blue and black fiber (Object's colors?). Concealing these peculiarities is no longer possible. Awaiting the Council inspection. Preparing for last-ditch measures. Tep's mission must be carried out."

...

November 25, 965

"Most of the staff tried to escape the complex. I destroyed the portal net after the Council agents arrived. Now they are all locked in here with me... The Astral storms won't let them fly Astral ships for the next two weeks, but still I sabotaged all the reactors - just in case. They will be able to leave the allod, but will inevitably explode in the Astral. The mentalists have already started brainwashing the staff. They must have received an order to carry out the full cleanup. Yesterday they saw one of the blue-eyed "returnees". He resisted and was destroyed at the spot... One of the mentalists has turned into a slobbery imbecile. That's interesting."

...

December 4, 965

...this entry breaks off abruptly. Something must have happened while it was written.

"The mentalists tried to get inside my head, too, but much to my surprise, they couldn't. They just couldn't. It had them puzzled, and me, too. I'm writing it being "arrested in quarters" in my room. The cult won't help me. We are too weak yet. Looks like I will ha..."

...

January 14, 966

"I don't remember the last month. Since the previous entry everything was as in a fog. Today I woke up in the middle of an empty corridor, surrounded by my former colleagues. Those blue eyes and the ringing silence. They didn't bother me though. I was calm. But what has happened in that month?"

...

January 15, 966

"The Mechanoids are dragging the dead bodies from all over the complex and throw them into the Astral. Is that how they get rid of the evidence? Wrecks of the Astral ships are floating over the allod - they tried to escape anyway... Idiots. For now, I haven't come across a single living (sentient) being on the whole territory of the complex. But I've seen Nezeb's stamp on a document in my office. The Council has shut down the whole research. The complex exists no more. The ghost complex. And I am its only inhabitant."

January 1, 1000

"I can hear exalted voices coming from nowhere. The new millennia. The first day. Oh, this is so important. I am making an entry just to mark that. I should keep the track of time. Tick tack. It is so slow. I can keep up with it, even on my rusty prostheses. I think Tep was supposed to come in the past millennia. Or the next one? I don't remember."

...

June 5, 1010

"Here he is. Speak of the devil, hahahahaha!!! I offered to show him to the shower - he's been lying in the coffin for ages... He looked at me as if I was an idiot, that damned egghead. And his Mechanoids are ugly, though they were built according to my schemes. And he himself looks... wrong. The Source is more beautiful. The Source told me that Tep was just a drop in the bucket. That Tep was useless. I should drive Tep away from our home. He has nothing to do with this place."

...

June 12, 1010

"It's all smoking and shaking! I think Tep is angry. I never thought he could scream like that. It got really frightening at some point. Maybe he was practicing? I need to practice, too (will start tomorrow after lunch). The bad news is that the Source wasn't able to resist him. So if it were not for my Mechanoids, it would be dead by now. You need to say: Thank you, Negus Jeeg. Thank you for being here."

October 5, 966

"I heard Nezeb died. I don't know who told me that, but I know it. That's amusing. I wanted to drink some champagne, but it's bad for my prostheses. I gave it to one of the blue-eyed. I think he liked it. I taught him to say "Glory to Tep!" Now he wanders around and mumbles it."

...

A summer month, 973

"He is silent. Everybody is silent. I am alone. A nice day."

...

New Year's Eve, 977

"Animals who call themselves Pridens have just broke in. They babble something about some Shoom branch and poke the Mechanoids with their hammers and sticks. Luckily, I have switched them off long ago."

...

January 14, 978 (as the furry ones say)

"I don't understand half of their savage words, but I like them (especially their forked cloaks!). The blue-eyed don't seem to notice them. Which means the Object doesn't care about their presence. But I have an idea."

...

June 2, 978

"Well, Tep can be proud of me. The tribe has left, determined to wipe out their home allod. I never knew I am so good at public speeches. Or was it the champagne? Ah, no... I've run out of it long ago."

...

Idontcarewhatdayitis, 986

"Perfection. I've achieved it. I've got nothing to eat, so I don't. It is easier than it seems - the blue-eyed know."

...

Lost track. Need to find it.

"I've cloned a deer. Just for the laughs. And food, of course. I don't think the blue-eyed are tasty, especially the wires."

A crystal as the source of the mutation? It can't be!

Yes, I can sense that it radiates some energy, but I fail to recognize its nature. If it is magic, then it is really unusual. But I have no doubt that this crystal was extracted from the meteorite at the bottom of the lake and transported to the Bestiary. What does it mean? It means two things!

The first thing is, the crystal was the key subject of the scientists' research. Maybe the constant exposure to its radiation caused the unexpected consequences.

The second thing, we don't know for sure whether the experiment failed, or was successful. The Bestiary has been abandoned for too long, and we don't know whether the mutated animals were bred on purpose, or the mutation was a side effect.

You know... I think you should speak to someone who knows more about technology and magic than anyone in Sarnaut. To Catherina!
Hickut, you say? Let me see... Oh, it is indeed. Finally I have something to do. Give me a couple of minutes, I will translate it.

Where did you get it?! Give it to me now, I must... Oh, sorry! I'm still a little bit out of my head after that Leper disaster...

Yes, I know something about this crystal. Long ago, I saw a shard like this one. It was tiny. The man who gave it to me told me that he had found it in a wrecked ship, full with withered bodies of Zem. I suppose those were Tep cultists - those Arisen who believe in the Light would have resurrected.

My research showed that the stone was emitting an unknown energy of such an enormous power that it subjugated and altered all other known magical fields. I was trying to figure it out for a very long time and could find no proper use for it, so I decided to implement it in one of my mechanisms as an element of the stand-by energy contour. That device was left on Eclipse... Oh, no, you destroyed it in the fight with my faithful captain Krivov!
What has brought you to my chamber? Don't waste my time!

You think this crystal caused the mutation? It is hard to believe that. Those mutations are random, there are no two similar cases, so I think it would be more accurate to call it modification - a deliberate interference into the living organisms - rather than mutation.

I think you should talk to Herbert. He knows more about these things.
Good day. How may I help you?

Obviously, we are facing a source of a tremendous unknown power. No wonder Tep wanted to acquire it. But why did he leave Ferris? Why didn't he take the Object? What has transformed the scientists? Why has no one ever heard of the "Gates" Project? There are so many questions...

We need to study all the records! The scientists must have kept logs and made reports. We need to find out what our predecessors knew to keep surveying!

quests: Light in the End of the Tunnel

t:
When I entered the vessel, an unknown power just broke my will. I stopped feeling my body! As if it didn't exist anymore; it fell into tiny particles and turned into a flow of information. And the cold tentacles started stirring those particles, sculpting a new me out of them!

And my consciousness... As if it was smashed against a clean white wall and left a distinct impression on it. I could see my own memory, I swear! I could remember everything that happened to me since I was born, every little detail... It was beautiful. But then something separated us, and I returned to my body, feeling as weak and tired as I was before. A terrible feeling, I must admit.
Oh, my head... I think my decision was a little too hasty.

I don't remember a thing... After I fell through the floor, the last thing that I saw was that giant vessel with a strange creature inside of it falling right at me. Then - only darkness...

The first thing that I saw after I woke up - you and Herbert. So I don't know more than you do. This is scary. What has happened to me?!
What are you doing here? What am I doing here?!
I still can't believe in what happened. That freak stole my body, stole my memory... He stole me from me!

I think we should go down and try to capture the crazy Arisen, and as for our clones... I think it would be the best to destroy them. Clones are unnatural! I almost lost my mind when I saw myself!

I wonder how did that maniac learn to clone. Clones, Mechanoids looking like Tep's servants... That's too much for an Imperial lab, don't you think? The Object really bothers me. We need to find out as much as possible about it, and to do so, we need to get to our mad experimenter.

Yes, I could see right away that you're one of ours.

Want me to tell you about the Demonologists' place in this world?

It was a miracle that we managed to persuade Yasker to let us open an office in the capital.

Now it's headed by Svetlana Demina, a close friend of mine. If you can get off this island and get to Nezebgrad - find her, she will explain what to do next.

Well, my advice is simple: do not neglect your gift. Use it. We can take many forms - choose one you like and follow your path.
Come closer, get some of that Patronage blessing!

What? What are you on about? I think that demon hit you too hard. There are no orc psionicists! You're just a weird shaman, hah.

And you should probably keep quiet about your... abilities.

May the Light bless you!

Once you are done with the ritual of Patronage, talk to me.

Oh, I see what you've experienced makes you wonder about things!

So what would you like to know?

Grokh shagrak! I wish Agrus knew... He will burn you!
I find Orb. You save me before. I must give it to you.
[You toss the journal back and leave.]

[You open the last pages of the diary and read]:

It's day 7 since I became a captain again.

It looks like we spent our last money yesterday, haha. Well, the guys wanted to go to that brothel with the hottest girls! And they had plenty of drinks on offer. But we have no money now. I need to think.

Day 9.

The crew is sober and angry. I've been thinking about ways to make money. No one needs June artifacts anymore. And the Empire no longer buys elven girls! Their clubs hire them now, so everything is voluntary. We tried mining etherium, but an Octulhu almost got us, so not doing that again. I had to think long and hard afterwards, even got a headache.

Day 12.

The guys keep suggesting ideas, each weirder than the last. Build our own allod? Every hobo has one now. Go to the Pirate Bay? They say it's even worse there now. Zirka keeps saying we should've accepted that contract from Korleone. But I promised that... that hero named  that we're done with that sort of thing. And it's too dangerous on Umoir now.

Day 13.

I heard from some elf that there's an island where you can hunt these creatures! What was it... Horse Woods? Drowning Woods? Let's go there.

Day 14.

We went to that island, and true enough, it was swarming with those beasts. We filled the hold to the brim. But that place, Drowsy Woods, is a very strange one. The guys felt something there. It was like someone was whispering. Luring them into the thickets. We cast off quickly. And Grunt, the idiot, said someone had sneaked aboard the ship. The drunkard's seeing things already.
You see before you the slightly singed journal of the ship's captain.

[It looks like the notes in this diary are more than five years old.

You open Harat's diary and read]:

The world has never seen a creature as perfect as a dragon. I have always tried to understand them. Alas, these days dragons are rare...

I have searched for them for many years. I perfected my skills, gained new knowledge. I read manuscripts of long-dead elven magisters in the ruins of allods that were destroyed a long time ago...

Eventually I became the best in my field. I get hired by Great Mages who thirst for their Blood. Dragon blood holds immense power! Someday I'll be able to wield it.

Yesterday I was offered a contract of my dreams. Catherina, the Great Mage of Umoir, charged me with the task of catching two dragons. I know where I'll find what I need. Dragons Soliskar the Wise and Agrus the Callous concealed themselves from human eyes after the well known events that took place in the Dead City. I managed to learn where they went with their dragon army. It's the allod Heart of Fire, their old dwelling and secret refuge.

I have a team. Goblins are despicable creatures that no one would miss. Many of them will die, but it will be enough to set up a trap.

I will track down and catch the dragons! Catherina let me in on her plan and granted me a part of her power. The world has never seen a creature as perfect as a dragon. It would pain me to sacrifice them. I wish there was another way to break the Seal and set the Creator free.
[You see before you a book with the owner’s name on it: Arat]

You carefully open the book and read the logs for the last dates:

Haregon – 20

Gulper – 15

Corrupted Owl – 10

Mutant Toad –  8

Taksa – 5

Werebear – 2

Agitated Toad – 1 That’s enough of them, what kind of idiot caught one of those?!

All from Drowsy Wood island. Hunter  Grunt.
[You see before you a singed book with the inscription “Inventory”.]
[You set the journal back down and leave.]

[You open the flight log to the last pages and read]:

Day 15 of the flight.

We are flying to sell our catch. Everything seems fine.

Day 16.

Everything is the same as yesterday. The animals are restless in their cages as if they know we are taking them far away.

Day 17.

Grunt came and said someone nicked the keys to the cages. Idiot! He lost them himself, probably... but we need to go check that out.
[You see before you a very messy “Flight Log”.]
[You set the journal back and leave.]

[You open the journal to the last pages and read]:

Entries on the final days:

They sent us to this forsaken island, I remember reading about it. No one goes there, absolutely no one. They say things named Tristesse used to live here and they were cursed or something... I know how to set a code lock or fix a generator, but catch beasts... I need to get away from these idiots in one piece...

Next entry:

We found Jo dead. He was pale as snow. I have no idea who could have even done it.

Next entry:

Zyrka also didn’t make it through the night. The entire team awoke to terrible screams. Had the entrance to the hold barricaded shut. Someone is hiding in there. And it’s no beast. We're flying back to Umoir, maybe they’ll help us there.

Next entry:

Awoke to screams on the lower deck today. Looks like something broke free, and we are steadily losing altitude for some reason. I have nothing to lose, so I’ll try jumping. Maybe the canopies will soften my fall and I’ll survive. Or maybe I’ll die.
[You see before you a surprisingly neat journal for a goblin.]

It's all very interesting and might help us... But we'll deal with that later. Alas, we have serious problems now.

There's too many undead under our command now, and they... started getting out of control. We should've prepared for such consequences, but we didn't. We handled it ourselves at the Outpost, but no one can protect the villages in the area. I'm too weak, and it's taking all my strength to keep the rest of the undead in check.

They plan to attack the nearest village, so they are gathering on the outskirts... Target the strongest of them – if they fall, the rest will follow. Protect the villages, and I'll stay here and take a break. I'll need to examine the crash site, perhaps you missed something. Once you're done, find me at the mill. There might be something else we can do.
First tell me what you learned here.
The mutilated body of a goblin who died doing his duty, slain by the claws of some creatures.
All the blood has been sucked out of this goblin shaman. The poor thing didn’t have time to cast a spell.
No doubt this haregon died in the jaws of a taksa. Predator and prey, even in these strange conditions.
A gulper was thrashed by frightened haregons. The leper animal food chain is not very orderly.
You see before you the dried corpse of a goblin soldier. He died fighting for... Money?
The taksa’s body is covered with lacerations from something’s claws and traces of melee weapon blows. Poor thing...
Where are we going to idle and drink now?
The worker grumbles and pokes around with an unsatisfied look at the heap of metal that was very recently an airship.
Excellent. I can always count on you. It crashed in the west of the forest. I’ll mark it on the map for you.

Not some ship, the Goblins' ship.

I don't care about them, but I have a few questions.

First – why are they here? We had an agreement that they wouldn't set foot on Umoir again.

Second – why did it crash here? Goblins might not be the most skilled astralonauts, but they are not that bad. Something happened here.

Anyway, just find out what happened, . You're an expert in these things.

Listen, thinking is not your job...!

You are right, but it doesn't matter how close this army is. We must be aware of what's happening around us. Perhaps these things are connected. Let's call it a premonition.

Besides, this is Catherina's domain, and her word is law here. And so is mine while I have her confidence. In short, don't argue with me. The sooner you get this done, the better.
It’s so dark and pretty here!

Did you find it after all?! Excellent, give it here...

The principle is quite simple: if I find out how it all started, then I can figure out how to reverse it. Make her sentient again... It’s possible we could even create a universal antidote against vampirism!

Now go talk to Zayan, . We need to do something with these Templars. Now we definitely can’t lose Annette...
There is no time to waste.

It's hard to begin a book from a blank page. I've been chewing on my quill over a blank scroll for a solid hour, not knowing where to start.

The thing is, I have a diary everyone knows about. A printing house made a mistake and printed way too many first pages, and just a few of the last ones. There was this scribe that put down my story about Umoir. I didn't write it myself.

My long-standing master Skrakan summoned me the other day. He said, "Danas, you've been though a lot, it's time to retire. Write a chronicle of your adventures."

I said, I'd rather fight than scribble!

And he went, oh no, no, no, buddy, you're tired. Settle down. The tower's all yours.

The Tower, you know. So be it! It's a nice cozy place full of lovely company. I enjoy my stay here. But I have no idea what to write!

I was thinking... Obviously, I can't write about Skrakan's secrets. I know better than to spill his beans, you know. I can write about places I visited.

I could come up with a guide to Allods! Perhaps, some traveler wants to follow my footsteps.

First things first. There were three of us. Firstly, there was me, Danas. Then there was my loyal friend Naira, and Fergard, the wizard. We also had Brian the Knight, but since then our paths have separated, although we see him a lot. Rud Glaen, the elf we saved near the Skytower, was traveling on some elven business. He loved secrets and mysteries and had a lot of names and faces. As to Reniesta... well, that's just too sad.

Some might ask, how many years has it been since you saved Skrakan? Two hundred. Others might say, it's not true. Come on, no human can live for two hundred years, it's the elven way.

I agree. Ordinary people can't live for two hundred years. Unless they're Great Mage's Ambassadors. Mages themselves live long lives, you know.

Yes, the three of us became Skrakan's Ambassadors after we defeated the Demon. It was his gift. We could travel all over Astral and live our long lives.

Everyone has Ambassadors. Loyal friends. Or servants. Tensess had them. Nezeb also has them. Perhaps, you've heard the name Vlad, well, he's the one.

Skrakan didn't force us to serve him. Besides, we were still at the Imperial service for Valir IV and Tensess. But somehow it happened that we traveled a lot on Skrakan's missions.

I told you how surprised I was to see representatives of our two states work together on Nea.

There's another place in Sarnaut where the gap between Kania and Xadagan doesn't exist.

It's the Ark allod, an amazing place, governed by the Great Mage Erast.

Originally, it was a small kingdom in south-western Kania. Nezeb's conquest spared Ark when he brought the Ugra hordes down on our southern frontier. However, it was cut off from mainland Kania.

Historically Kanian, Ark is full of Xadagan. Then again, they trade with Xadagan, but there's a small elven enclave in the Kingdom, where elven craftsmen produce armor and brew potions.

Ark is a hodgepodge with a bit of this and a bit of that. Erast thought himself independent, but he didn't forget to show respect to Nezeb. After all, he was his closest neighbor.

The Xadaganian Emperor didn't dare to conquer Ark either. The trade was good, and they didn't need such a small patch of land, anyway.

It's become a real heaven after the Cataclysm. They don't have to pay taxes neither to Kania nor to Xadagan. There's no military recruitment. Live and let live, you know. There are no real threats in Ark. A handful of trolls and Kobolds in local caves never come out to the valley.

People are cheerful. It's a wild mixture of Kanians and Xadaganians, you can't tell one from another. There are also elves. I've already mentioned the House de Ark.

Erast's valley is a truly amazing sight. Small mountain rivers flow around beautiful gardens, full of roses.

There's still a place in the troubled world where you can enjoy your life. Eventually, I had to return to Umoir. And now I'm here to tell you this amazing story. Sorry if it wasn't smooth. I couldn't tell you everything, but my story is true.
You haven't found this page yet. Try looking at the Border Outpost.

Let me start with a story about my motherland, Kanian Archipelagos.

Our land is beautiful, for sure. Full of meadows and forests, lakes and mountains. There's nothing we don't have.

First of all, there's the capital city. Kania.

Where do allod names come from? They're named after towers of Great Mages that hold together these lands. Our tower was named after the city. And the city was named after the Emperor, who founded it. Initially, it was Qwator, but over time that has changed to Kania.

This is how it began. Prince Qwator founded the city. Today the city is called Kania. It's build around the Qwator tower on the Kanian Archipelago. I hope you haven't lost track.

Our capital city is the best. There's the Tensess Tower, and we also have a palace, Schleherloht. It's hard to pronounce, but it's a real word in Elvish. There are all kinds of mansions around the palace. Merchants, craftsmen, and nobility live there. A little farther away are gardens.

We only have one large city. Our people aren't fond of living in cities, but Kanian Archipelagos are full of villages. There are Greenvilles and Springfields, villages for all tastes. I grew up in one of them.

People inhabit the western side of the allod. They leveled forests and turned them into fertile fields. The allod is divided into counties where the nobility rule. We have Zalessky county, Seversky county, and Nezhinsky county, each with a noble family. Counties are divided by hills or mountains, or sometimes even roads.

A number of lakes lie in the center of the allod. We have lakes Blue, Cold, White, and Mud, to every taste! The capital is located at the shore of the biggest lake.

The eastern side of the allod is forested and less populated. It's a source of wood and game. You can find Amberwood and Birchwoods there. As I said, there aren't too many people, just a couple of villages. The road leads through Birchwoods to Valir county, the Emperor's holiday residence. The road goes further on to Zagorie. This is where the wilderness lies.

There are wilder areas, thought, to the north. It's called Siveria. It's as cold as Lightwood, inhabited mainly by orcs and goblins.

They could show up in Birchwoods to rob caravans but they got beat up. Eventually, they learned their lesson: we don't see them around any more. No one risks going to Siveria, either.

Today Kanian Archipelagos are vast and abundant. Taxes we have to pay aren't all that high, so there's nothing to complain about.

Today I will tell you about the Grok allod. We visited it when Skrakan wanted us to deliver a message to Claude de Vevre, the elven Great Mage of that allod.

Elves would rather stay away from people, as you know. They like to keep their secrets to themselves. Besides, they aren't very fond of strangers. Although, you might know that they live on Umoir, as well. Somewhere beyond Al Rihat. They craft and trade, and earn their living. But that's a small House.

On the other hand, the House de Vevre is grand. I have no idea how they identify them. I hear, it's done at the Great Balls.

Anyway, elves on Grok aren't exactly open to strangers. They didn't trust me at first, either.

It's time to tell you a little about the allod. Grok is a vast steppe with just a few woods and mountains around the edges of the allod.

Elves of the House de Vevre live in the center of the allod in several medium-sized cities. Local soil doesn't really bear fruit, perhaps, due to cold winds and lack of rivers. Crops just don't want to grow!

Elves got their magic at hand, but apart from that, they also grow cattle, such as cows or sheep. They ride huge lions, who also help them herd and guard the cattle. The lions are, in fact, well-behaved and trained. They obey their masters like no one else!

Sounds idyllic, doesn't it? elves ride on lions and herd their cattle! Just wait. There's a problem that makes the elves' lives too hard. And that's orcs.

There's no end to them. Orcs inhabit the steppes on the allod outskirts. The House de Vevre is dreaming to get rid of them, but you can't just chase down an ork in the steppe.

Orcs ride huge rhinos and lizards. There's no way to catch them! They hunt... and eat elven cows. And not only cows. Trust me, you don't want to face the orcs without friends around.

That's exactly how we earned their trust, by the way. Did you guess? There was this lady that had to come out on her own and got kidnapped by the orcs. We had to follow her before it was too late. Naira is a great pathfinder and Fergard's a wizard. And me... well, I was the brute force.

We got to the orcish camp, killed the guards, and found the elf, tied to a pole. We set her free and fled! We ran as fast as we could.

Orcs followed, but we narrowly escaped.

That's how it happened.

Last time I told you about an elven allod where elves live alongside orcs, and now I'm going to tell you about an allod where elves reign over the land, and yet Kanians also live there.

Grok's Great Mage is Claude de Vevre, but Andis is controlled by his cousin - Catherine de Vevre...

Here's a de Vevre, there's a de Vevre, everywhere's a de Vevre. But you could really tell the difference, you know.

Originally, Andis was a Kanian region. Before the Black Night, it turned out that the only magic tower, the Andis tower, was occupied by the elf who wanted to live near her family.

Catherine did a great job of safeguarding the allod. She kept everyone alive. As soon as everything settled down, the elves started to introduce their own rules.

They chased away some local nobility. Some were tortured to death in prisons, others were banished from the allod.

Elves occupied their homes, redesigned them, and began harassing and oppressing the Kanians.

How? They took their lands, set up plantations, and forced the farmers to slave away there.

Taxation on its own can be hard enough, but this! People had no choice but to come to work at plantations. Otherwise they would have starved to death.

If your work is not up to their standards, they whip you. Hard.

Elves are good at keeping score. Nothing escapes their attention. There's no cutting corners with them. Eventually, people began to riot. They set fire to some things, robbed a mansion...

Elves never pardoned them. Everyone was executed.

This is how things are here. They'd never let us in unless we had an agreement with Claude. They never treated us well, though. The attitude was more like, "Puny humans! What are you doing here?"

I don't think you want to hear more about the situation. You must be curious about the allod. It's quite ordinary. Soil is rather fertile here. The climate is a little on the hot side, hotter than it is on the Kanian Archipelagos, but it's alright. It's a very green place. If it weren't for the elven tyranny, it could be heaven.

You probably want to ask me - have you been to Xadaganian allods, Danas?

I'll tell you the truth. I have. My duties took me to Igsh...

What can I say? Another prairie allod, but without orcs, for a change.

Dead Sea is its major feature. There was a real sea once, but when the astral split the ground, the sea leaked and poured into astral, like water from a cracked bucket.

Igsh has no cities. Only nomads wonder around prairies, patrol the roads, move horses and camels. As there are no orcs, crowds of goblins feel at ease. Xadaganians despise them, and would kill them whenever they can, but goblins are incredibly cunning and know how to hide. We completed our mission thanks to them.

The Great Mage's tower stands in the middle of prairies. The Igsh tower can't be compared to the Xadagan tower, the Emperor Nezeb's residence. Igsh is governed by his lapdog Cadyr.

Naira, Fergard, and I took greater interest in Baladur Port. It was a sea port years ago, but when the sea disappeared, the port fell into decay. Over time, something happened: sailors died and turned into ghosts.

We were looking for someone named Vlad. This weasel was born even before the Cataclysm. We knew that Igsh was his place of residence.

We were to meet the businessman Denis Korleone who corresponded with Vlad.

Everything went wrong. First thing on Igsh, we stumbled into an ambush. We fought our way through, but the Xadaganian patrol followed us closely.

It was a miracle that we could get to the former port and managed to persuade goblins to guide us through the system of underground channels. Denis, practically my namesake, was waiting for us. He gave us valuable information. The thing was, after Urd's death, Nezeb realized that he couldn't trust his ex-comrades: the Great Mages of Xadagan, who lived even before the Cataclysm. He decided to replace them. He needed some new apprentices, and when these would be ready to serve, he had to replace those who lost his trust with the new dogs, loyal and obedient.

This is why he needed Vlad, Nezeb's long-living Ambassador and his personal assassin, the head of a special squad called Nezeb Falcons. They were going to kill the Great Mages. Skrakan was worried. What could he do? Nothing. It was our mission.

After hearing my stories about the elves of the House de Vevre, you probably think that most elves are arrogant bastards.

But it's not true. Houses are very different.

The House de Doucer is the absolute opposite of many Houses. Perhaps, that's because they never had to share an allod.

Yoggor is the domain of the House de Doucer.

The bards are singing about Yrene, a united kingdom that elves used to have centuries ago. Many Houses have parted ways since then. Many of them settled in distant corners of Yul and founded small kingdoms. Those who survived the Cataclysm became elven allods.

Yoggor was a major elven allod. Gramon de Doucer was the Great Mage, an heir and apprentice of ancient elven mages, only a little weaker than Skrakan
.
He united those who ended up on his allod after the Black Night into a major House and thus restored the tradition of Great Houses. The remaining eight Great Houses were a part of it.

Yoggor is quite an unusual location: a magnificent forest full of tall trees. Most elves live in their own castles scattered all over the allod.

This allod is inhabited largely by elves. However, there are creatures that pose threat to lonely travelers. Animals, mostly, such as giant spiders and mantis. We had a fight or two here, I should tell you.

The House de Doucer members seemed friendlier than the elves I'd met before (and unlike our friend Rud Glaen, of course).

I can't tell you more about our mission, but Gramon was happy to receive a message from his old friend Skrakan and invited us to visit, like we did later.

We visited this quite unusual Xadaganian allod a little later.

At the time, Nezeb's Falcons were hunting down disloyal Great Mages... They took out Vodor of Arav, Kadir of Igsh, Rashid of Sulanger... The Xadaganian Emperor replaced them all with his loyal allies.

There were tragedies, of course. Allod Karakir vanished into astral, because the new Great Mage, appointed by Nezeb, couldn't hold what his predecessor, the Great Mage Jabbar, could...

Skrakan was very upset by what was going on. Many people in Kania were happy, though. Nezeb was weakening the Empire with his own hands!

However, Gorluxor from Yakhch liked it even less than Skrakan.

He was one of Skrakan's apprentices who sided with Nezeb during the Conquests. Gorluxor allied with Xadagan and gained absolute power in his lands, but it was no longer enough for his master.

Gorluxor came to Skrakan for help. He wanted to take revenge on Falcons, the mage killers.

Of course, this was our mission.

What can I tell you about Yakhch? It used to be an ordinary, unremarkable deserted allod. This is where the Druids came to plant the seed of the Great Tree in one of the oases.

None of the Great Mages knows what the Great Trees really are. The first of them grow somewhere on the Northern allod. They appeared on Yul much later when merchants managed to find some seeds.

In the Allod era, it turned out that the Trees granted solid protection against the Astral. Even a young sapling could save a big city. The Great Trees were planted everywhere! Alas, they don't always take root. Sometimes you can grow them, but sometimes they die.

Such tree grew on Kanian Archipelagos, but it withered on Umoir.

The Tree deeply affected Yakhch and the landscape. The desert turned into a dense forest, a real taiga. The climate has also changed: there were more downfalls, and it was colder.

I can't say the Xadaganians put much value on it. Yakhch became their major source of wood: they sent it over to different regions of their kingdom.

I suppose you know what happened to Gorluxor. It was hard, but we saved his skin. I faced Vlad myself when I had to fight his Falcons in the Yakhch tower. I sent the birdies back home. I have no idea what Gorluxor said to Nezeb, but there wasn't a single attempt to kill Gorluxor ever since.

Now that you know all about the elven and Xadaganian allods, I bet you would like to learn about your motherland Kania.

But that's the thing - Kania is right there, outside your window. Look! It's all about the same on the Kanian Archipelagos, in Forox, or Umoir.

Sure, there are distant corners like the frozen Lightwood, but people live the same lives there, even if they have to wear fur clothes.

I'm going to tell you about Scarge. It's Kanian, but it's different.

The Great Mage Smaragd the Emerald. He was a skilled craftsman even before the Cataclysm. He loved ancient mechanisms, especially those found in ancient ruins. There were people like Junes or Hickutians who were extremely skilled in engineering and devices.

Smaragd always wanted to breathe life into the non-living. Sometimes he succeeded, other times he failed, but over time, his skill grew. Remember the clock in the Archipelago capital? You know, the one that shows you little figurines dancing by themselves? They're Smaragd's creation, a gift to Tensess.

The three of us went to Scarge. It's full of miracles. I saw clockwork idols filled with gears and pinwheels. Whenever Smaragd's servants wind them, the idols start moving, bowing, and even trying to speak!

We also saw clockwork horses with pinwheels. We rode one of these to the Tower.

So many miracles! And the Tower is spinning, clicking, and clacking.

We visited Scarge to settle a minor affair, but then Smaragd told us a sad story. The local rulers had a daughter, a pretty, smart and lovely girl. A witch kidnapped her and hid somewhere. The Great Mage wanted us to find the girl. If I wanted to tell you all the details, I would have to write a big book! The one thing I can tell you, though, is that we found her. She was a sorceress and became Smaragd's apprentice later.
